## Body

Price the whole lifecycle, not only the queue method.

A native hold's recovery method is one write transaction, but every recovered body's delivery.outcome is separately persisted before the renewed edge. These writes run under the global native lock and broadcast through existing subscribers. Include them in edge cost; no new timer or launch site does not mean no added write work.

The 64 limit is checked only on a new held-send admission. Reconciliation parks an existing backlog without that cap; the two-hour deadline bounds recovery eligibility, not job-row retention. Count/selection uses the recipient/state index and still visits failed-row history. Recovery's inherited live-duplicate predicate has no kind/recipient equality and can visit global live jobs for each recovered body. Failed holds themselves stay outside the indexed claim preflight and next-due timer.

Successful recovery is a negative expiry decision: no notice is owed. If that decision is not durably settled, the 24-hour park sweep repeats audit/admission/FYI reads and a no-op expiry write transaction at every sweep after the original deadline. Budget windowed event volume, not current holds alone.

Evidence: PR314 head 2ad9e18ca43c1b55fed3b44d962303d9e75f31e6; queue.rs:775-880, delivery/mod.rs:840-982, park_notice.rs:301-333,459-510; CI44889108768/job136800807802/artifact14701003627, fourteen focused cases passed. Exact-source SQLite3.54.1 probe with all48 migrations: 64-body recovery 28,961 VM instructions versus1,180,960 with2,000 unrelated live rows; select/count grow with expired history; 65 pre-existing queued bodies park as65 holds. Synthetic query work is not deployed CPU proof.

magicWand: a deterministic complete-path transaction receipt plus a regression that a recovered hold's expiry becomes terminally not-owed. Reuse existing sweep/audit machinery rather than add a new scheduler.
